name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator and is a subtype of T, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that it is safe to coerce self to T after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx), provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Multiple successive coercions to supertypes are permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.
expression: The supplied DSL cannot express this requirement: it exposes only an opaque type handle, with no predicates for coercion safety, trait implementation, subtyping, or method-call history.
